text:
incident-bot: ALERT: gpu-node-34 reporting repeated Xid errors and ECC correctable spikes. Priority P1. Paging on-call for gpu-infra. https://redwood.internal/alerts/4789001234 :rotating_light:
Olivia: I'm on it. seeing drive-by spikes in prometheus, memory-correctable-ECC counter jumping on node-34. routing impact: ~8% inference 5xx from serving-runtime in prod-us-east-1.
Michael: confirmed. traces show increased latency + some container restarts. which tenant(s) hit?
Sana: reports show KSERVING jobs and runtime containers on node-34 evicted/restarted. KV cache thrash for long-lived chat sessions.
Olivia: oncall plan: cordon node, drain non-critical pods, migrate serving traffic off node, attempt a driver restart. if driver restart fails, plan for node reboot and notify customers.
Jeremy: agreed. telemetry shows Xid 126 and multiple "NVRM: GPU memory ECC error" lines in dmesg. attaching sample logs: 
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 126, PID=3782, GPU=0, Channel ID=00000000, engine=0x01
[ 1234.567912] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU memory ECC corrected error detected
[ 1234.568001] containerd: runtime v2: container exited with signal 11
[ 1234.568500] nvidia: invoking reset handler for GPU 0
```
Olivia: running quick impact check: routing rules already fallback to dedicated-pool-1 for cold starts, but sticky sessions still hit the affected node causing errors. Michael, can you lift circuit breaker for chat-api to force route away?
Michael: on it. patching routing: set weight 0 for node-34 endpoint in envoy via /ops/route API.
ops-bot: Deploy request accepted: /ops/route set-weight node-34 0 -> rollback in 30m if not acked.
Sana: starting live mitigation: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-34` then `kubectl drain gpu-node-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60` to evacuate serving pods safely. will watch replica readiness.
Jeremy: while drain runs, I'll attempt `systemctl restart nvidia-driver` on node-34. if restart fails, we'll attempt node reboot. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-driver-reset.
Olivia: if driver restart triggers cascading restarts, prioritize preserving evaluation and core serving; we can tolerate some background batch jobs moving.
Michael: rolling routing change applied. telemetry shows 92% of traffic now off node-34. error rate down to ~1.5% but still some transient 5xx from sticky sessions.
Sana: drain in progress: evicted 18 pods so far, 6 left (3 are stateful). I'll coordinate with app owners on those stateful pods.
Jeremy: driver restart result: `Failed to reset device` on first try. trying soft unload/reload: `modprobe -r nvidia_uvm && modprobe nvidia_uvm` then `systemctl restart nvidia-docker`.
Olivia: heads-up: customer-impact comms needed? low-latency customers may see degraded throughput for experiments. Ops: prep status page update.
ops-bot: Status update draft prepared: "Investigating GPU driver resets causing errors for a subset of inference requests in us-east-1. Traffic rerouted; mitigation in progress." link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/4789001234
Jeremy: soft unload succeeded, but kernel logs still show repeated ECC corrections; driver reports degraded state. scheduling node reboot in 5 min unless objections.
Michael: agree reboot. also trigger health-checks to force new warmup paths.
Sana: checkpointing KV cache eviction for sessions on draining pods to avoid double-replay. Taking a snapshot of problematic session keys and marking as rehydrate on target nodes.
Olivia: handoff: I'm switching to second-line escalation. Michael will take lead for the next 2 hours during reboot + verification. I'll stay looped for customer escalation. :thumbsup:
Michael: taking lead. Actions list: 1) reboot node-34 2) post-reboot vendor-driver update if logs show same Xid pattern 3) keep routing weight 0 until telemetry stable 4) run regression evals on a sample prompt set.
Jeremy: node reboot initiated. `reboot` issued.
incident-bot: SYSTEM: reboot job queued and executed on gpu-node-34. Please monitor node join events.
Sana: node back online — kubelet re-registered, GPU visible but `nvidia-smi` shows ECC corrected counters non-zero. running stress test and smoke eval.
Michael: smoke evals: token throughput within SLAs, small tail latencies improved. error rate back down to baseline ~0.2%.
Olivia: postmortem notes to collect: dmesg logs pre/reboot, driver version, kernel version, workload mix, pod distribution, and whether any model-quantization change correlated. assign to Jeremy + Sana.
ops-bot: Noted. Creating incident ticket: INC-2026-4789001234 with severity P1, assignees: Jeremy, Sana, Michael.
Michael: next steps: keep node in quarantine (weight 0) for 24h, collect ECC telemetry, consider proactive cordon for siblings showing early counters. If ECC continues, plan hardware replacement via datacenter ops.
Olivia: handoff complete. leaving notes in runbook and tagging #customer-bridge for impacted enterprise accounts.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, traffic rerouted, node rebooted. Monitoring for 1h.
Jeremy: final note before I drop: saw an odd pattern — corrected ECC counts spike every ~90s before Xid. I'll add that to telemetry alert thresholds.
Sana: thanks team. I'll run a focused eval against the warm cache scenarios and report regressions.
Michael: closing on-call shift. will escalate to hardware replacement if corrected ECC continues.
Olivia: thanks everyone. re-open thread if we see reoccurrence. :white_check_mark:
